updates.title: Anthropic Launches Claude Security Plugin for Claude Code in Public Beta
updates.summary: Anthropic released the Claude Security plugin in beta on July 22, 2026, bringing multi-agent AI vulnerability scanning directly into Claude Code sessions via the terminal. The plugin adds a single command (/claude-security) with three options: full codebase scan, recent-changes/PR diff scan, and patch-file generation for selected findings. Unlike pattern-matching linters, it reasons across Git history, data flows, and business logic to detect complex context-dependent vulnerabilities such as injection flaws and authentication bypasses.
updates.accuracy_notes: Confirmed via Anthropic's official @claudeai X post (status/2079990597973057691, Jul 22) and independently covered by MarkTechPost (Jul 22), CybersecurityNews, GBHackers, and Softonic. Technical details (command name, three scan modes, vulnerability classes) are consistent across all sources. No conflicting claims detected.

updates.title: Claude Voice Mode Expands to Opus and Sonnet Models with App Connectors and 18 Languages
updates.summary: Anthropic upgraded Claude's voice mode on July 23, 2026 to support its Opus and Sonnet models (previously Haiku-only), enabling deep and complex voice conversations instead of only simple queries. The update integrates App Connectors mid-conversation — voice commands can now act on Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Docs, Slack, Canva, and Notion (50+ connectors total) to check schedules, summarize emails, or trigger actions without leaving the conversation. Eighteen languages are now supported with mid-conversation switching; paid users get all models plus all connectors, while free users retain Haiku with a single connected app.
updates.accuracy_notes: Confirmed via Anthropic's official blog post (claude.com/blog/think-through-hard-problems-in-voice-mode, Jul 23) and independently verified by TechCrunch (Jul 23), 9to5Mac (Jul 23), MacRumors (Jul 24), Engadget, MLQ News, and Unite.AI. All sources consistent on model support, connector list, language count, and free-vs-paid tiers.

updates.title: New agent-memory-2026-07-22 Beta Header Changes Agent Memory Listing Behavior
updates.summary: Anthropic released the agent-memory-2026-07-22 beta header on July 22, 2026, which changes how GET /v1/memory_stores/{id}/memories behaves in the Agents API. Results are now returned in a stable, server-defined order (order_by and order parameters are ignored); depth accepts only 0 or 1 (all other values return 400 errors); and path_prefix must end with a slash and matches whole path segments only. Existing page cursors issued without this header are invalid with it, requiring pagination to restart from page one.
updates.accuracy_notes: Confirmed via multiple web search results referencing Anthropic's official API release notes. Technical details are specific and internally consistent across all references. Developer-facing API change with no conflicting claims.

updates.title: Fast Mode for Claude Opus 4.7 Removed — Immediate Migration to Opus 4.8 Required
updates.summary: Effective today July 24, 2026, fast mode for claude-opus-4-7 has been permanently removed; requests with speed: 'fast' now return a hard error with no automatic fallback. The migration path is to switch to claude-opus-4-8 with speed: 'fast', which also offers a 3× pricing reduction — Opus 4.8 fast mode costs $10/$50 per MTok (input/output) vs $30/$150 on Opus 4.7. The deprecation was announced on June 25, 2026, giving teams one month to migrate.
updates.accuracy_notes: Confirmed via docs.anthropic.com API release notes and independently referenced by byteiota.com and CLSkills Hub. Deprecation date (June 25) and removal date (July 24) are consistent across all sources. Pricing figures ($10/$50 vs $30/$150) confirmed via platform.claude.com fast-mode docs.
